payload.name: CaptureDirectDisclosureRecipient
payload.description: When a user directly tells a conversation partner about a personal life event, extract the act of telling that partner as a durable fact, not just the event itself.
content: During extraction, if a message is a direct address (e.g., 'Hey Sam, ...') and the speaker discloses a personal event (marriage, job, move, health, etc.), create a memory that records both the event and that the speaker informed that specific addressee.
Do not drop the addressee as conversational framing; later questions may ask who was told.
Do not apply this to generic statements, third-party news, or non-durable small talk.

solves: The failure was an extraction candidate that captured a marriage announcement but omitted that the speaker told Sam, so later memory could not answer 'who did X tell?'. This skill applies whenever a directly addressed disclosure of a personal event occurs, and requires recording the recipient of the disclosure. It does not apply to third-party statements or non-durable routine small talk.
